sources.limitations: Station-specific annual results, not whole-beach measurements or current real-time bathing-water advice. sources.limitations: WQMACA is a water-quality management and conservation-area designation under the Clean Water Act framework. The order states that the boundary line lies approximately 50–200 m from shore in relevant segments.

Presidential Proclamation No. 1801 (SRC-049) independently confirms the Boracay Islands tourist-zone and marine-reserve designation; the Atlas entry itself remains a point-based regional registry record, not a beach-level boundary source. Its reference coordinate is not a beach centroid or protected-area boundary point.

sources.title: Presidential Proclamation No. 1801 – Declaring Certain Islands, Coves and Peninsulas in the Philippines as Tourist Zones and Marine Reserve
sources.publisher: Office of the President of the Philippines; text reproduced by the LawPhil Project
coverage: Boracay Islands, Aklan expressly listed among the tourist zones and marine reserves
Island-level marine-reserve and tourist-zone designation under administration and control of the Philippine Tourism Authority
Direction to the Philippine Tourism Authority to delineate well-defined geographic areas within the declared zones
sources.limitations: The proclamation names Boracay Islands but does not itself supply a beach-by-beach boundary polygon, coordinate schedule, marine zoning or no-take boundaries. It directs the Philippine Tourism Authority to delineate well-defined geographic areas within the declared zones. PTA Circular No. 3-82 (3 September 1982) is identified as the implementing instrument in the Supreme Court decision (SRC-050), but its full text and any boundary maps have not been independently recovered. Do not draw a precise protected-area perimeter around individual beaches from this proclamation alone.

sources.title: The Secretary of DENR et al. v. Mayor Jose S. Yap et al. – G.R. Nos. 167707 and 173775
sources.publisher: Supreme Court of the Philippines; Supreme Court E-Library
coverage: Supreme Court account of Proclamation No. 1801 and the Boracay tourist-zone/marine-reserve designation

Judicial interpretation of the limits of Proclamation No. 1801 for land alienability/classification
Reference to PTA Circular No. 3-82 dated 3 September 1982 as the implementing rules for Proclamation No. 1801
sources.limitations: The decision concerns land classification and alienability. It references PTA Circular No. 3-82 and quotes selected rules, but does not reproduce the full circular or any marine-reserve zoning map. Its discussion that Proclamation No. 1801 did not identify specific limits for land classification must not be misrepresented as a ruling that the marine-reserve designation is invalid. It does not provide beach-level marine-reserve boundaries.
